 Ather Energy Turns Profitable in Q2 FY27 as Revenue Reaches Rs 1,464 Cr 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor
 Oct 26, 2026 
 Oct 26, 2026 / 
 118 
 / 3 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 -->
 -->
 Electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 1.3 crore in the September quarter of FY27, compared with a net loss of Rs 154.1 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The company had posted a net loss of Rs 51.1 crore in the June quarter of FY27. 
 Ather Energy's operating revenue increased 62.9 percent year-on-year to Rs 1,464.2 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 898.9 crore in the year-ago period. On a sequential basis, revenue grew 20.3 percent from Rs 1,216.9 crore in Q1 FY27. 
 Including other income of Rs 62.7 crore, the company's total income reached Rs 1,527 crore during the quarter, compared with Rs 940.7 crore in the corresponding period last year. 
 Despite reporting its first quarterly net profit in the period under review, Ather's operating revenue remained below its total expenses. The company's operating revenue was Rs 61.5 crore lower than its overall expenditure, highlighting the contribution of other income to its reported profitability. 
 The development follows an improvement in the company's operating performance in the June quarter, when Ather Energy reported positive earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) of Rs 9 crore. However, it continued to report a net loss of Rs 51.1 crore in Q1 FY27. 
 Ather's total expenses rose 39.4 percent year-on-year to Rs 1,526 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,094.7 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The increase was slower than the growth in operating revenue during the period. 
 Alongside its financial results, the electric vehicle manufacturer announced plans to expand its annual manufacturing capacity by a combined 2.25 lakh units across its existing Hosur facility and the upcoming Factory 3.0 in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra. 
 The planned capacity expansion is expected to support Ather Energy's manufacturing requirements as it continues to grow its electric two-wheeler business. 
 The latest results reflect an improvement in revenue growth and reported profitability, while the planned manufacturing expansion signals the company's focus on increasing production capacity to support its next phase of growth.

 Kapiva Revenue Nears Rs 465 Cr in FY26 as Offline Sales Grow 81 Pc 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 26, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 Ayurvedic wellness brand Kapiva reported a 36.5 percent year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 464 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 340 crore in FY25. Following 50 percent revenue growth in the previous fiscal year, the company continued expanding while keeping its losses broadly stable. 
 Including Rs 10 crore in non-operating income, Kapiva's total income reached Rs 474 crore in FY26. Founded in 2015, the company sells Ayurvedic nutrition and wellness products across categories such as diabetes management, liver health, women's hormonal health, energy, and sports nutrition. 
 Kapiva's total expenditure rose 31.2 percent to Rs 547 crore in FY26 from Rs 417 crore in FY25. Advertising and promotional expenses remained its highest cost, increasing 39.8 percent to Rs 260 crore from Rs 186 crore and accounting for nearly 48 percent of total expenditure. 
 Procurement costs grew 22.6 percent to Rs 117 crore, while employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 78 crore. Despite higher spending, losses remained relatively stable at Rs 72 crore, compared with Rs 69 crore in FY25. 
 Excluding employee stock option (ESOP) expenses of Rs 7.85 crore, the company's EBITDA margin improved to -14.8 percent from -18.7 percent a year earlier. Kapiva spent Rs 1.18 for every rupee of operating revenue generated. 
 The company has invested in expanding its product portfolio and offline distribution infrastructure, particularly in liver care, cholesterol management and women's hormonal health. 
 “During the last year, Kapiva has made significant investments in creating new categories (Liver Care, Cholesterol, Women’s Hormonal Health) and building infrastructure for offline distribution. These investments are likely to deliver substantial leverage in coming years which helps drive profitability,” a company spokesperson said. 
 In FY26, Kapiva's lifestyle diseases category grew 114 percent year-on-year, while daily wellness increased 66 percent and women's health rose 21 percent. Sports nutrition and energy recorded 5 percent growth. 
 Offline sales led channel expansion, growing 81 percent year-on-year. Marketplace revenue increased 34 percent, while the direct-to-consumer (D2C) channel grew 21 percent. The average order value on its D2C platform stood at approximately Rs 1,200, with repeat purchases contributing nearly 55 percent of D2C revenue. 
 Kapiva reported an annual recurring revenue (ARR) of approximately Rs 650 crore to Rs 700 crore and aims to achieve a low-single-digit positive EBITDA margin by Q4 FY27. 
 The company has raised around $90 million to date, including a $60 million Series D funding round led by 360 ONE Asset and Vertex Growth. Its revenue has grown approximately 93 percent over two years, from Rs 240 crore in FY24 to Rs 464 crore in FY26.

 Nutrifresh Plans Southern India Expansion With Rs 400 Cr FY27 Revenue Target 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 23, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 Indian controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) company Nutrifresh reported revenue of Rs 219.3 crore in FY26, registering a 51 percent increase from Rs 145.2 crore in FY25. The company is targeting Rs 400 crore in revenue for FY27, driven by farm capacity expansion, institutional funding and rising demand from quick-commerce platforms, modern retailers and hospitality businesses. 
 Founded in 2019, Nutrifresh has remained profitable since its inception. The company currently operates 83 acres of farmland and has an additional 105 acres under construction at Warwadi and Pisavare near Pune. The new facilities are expected to increase its production capacity as it prepares for the next phase of growth. 
 During FY26, Nutrifresh and Rural Enhancers Group signed a memorandum of understanding with the Maharashtra government to develop a 1,000-acre smart-agriculture project. The company also secured an initial tranche of Rs 90 crore from the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), forming part of a proposed Rs 400 crore investment to expand its controlled-environment agriculture infrastructure. 
 Nutrifresh supplies produce to more than 100 large business customers across the hotel, restaurant, modern retail and quick-commerce segments. Its client base includes Swiggy, Zepto, Flipkart Minutes, BigBasket, Reliance Fresh, Nature’s Basket, IHCL and Taj SATS. The company distributes its produce across 15 Indian states and international markets, including the UAE, Maldives and Singapore. 
 The company employs more than 650 people, with women accounting for 60 percent of its workforce. Women represent 80 percent of its farm-level employees and more than 43 percent of leadership positions. 
 For FY27, Nutrifresh expects its productive farmland footprint to nearly triple and is preparing to expand its operations across southern India. It is also scaling its Joint Farming model, which enables farmers to grow produce on their own land in partnership with the company. The approach is intended to increase production without requiring equivalent capital investment in company-owned farms. Nutrifresh has set a long-term ambition to support more than 25,000 farmers through this model. 
 Co-founder, CEO and Whole-Time Director Sanket Mehta attributed the company's growth to its proximity to urban markets, business-to-business distribution network and investments in crop-specific technologies. CFO and Whole-Time Director Ganesh Nikam highlighted disciplined capital allocation, investor support and strategic partnerships as important factors supporting the company's expansion. 
 With increasing revenue, additional farmland, and institutional funding, Nutrifresh is focusing on scaling its technology-led agricultural operations while maintaining profitability and expanding its supply network across India.

 {Funding Alert} Harajuku Tokyo Café Secures $3 Mn to Expand Japanese Food Business in India 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 23, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 Harajuku Tokyo Café, the Japanese food and beverage company operating Harajuku Tokyo Café and Harajuku Bakehouse, has raised $3 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by Zero W. The company plans to use the capital to expand its outlet network, strengthen its operational infrastructure, and enter additional Indian markets. 
 Existing investors Indian Angel Network (IAN) and Samved VC participated in the round through follow-on investments. New investors include Blume Founders Fund, Brijesh Parekh Family Office, Rahul Jain, co-founder of Epigamia, and others. 
 The latest funding follows a $2 million (Rs 19 crore) seed round raised in August 2025. The round was co-led by IAN and Samved VC, with participation from LetsVenture and venture debt fund Capitar Ventures. 
 Harajuku Tokyo Café is targeting revenue of Rs 100 crore in the current financial year. The fresh capital will support its next phase of growth as it expands across existing and new markets. 
 Founded in 2021 by Gaurav Kanwar, the company operates two food and beverage formats across Delhi NCR and Mumbai. Harajuku Tokyo Café is a full-service dining concept featuring conveyor-belt sushi and Tokyo-inspired interiors, while Harajuku Bakehouse operates as a quick-service format offering Japanese breads, desserts and savoury snacks. 
 The company has developed its menu and operating model in collaboration with chefs Asami Indo and Higuchi Nariaki, with a focus on introducing contemporary Japanese food to Indian consumers while building a platform for expansion. 
 Over the next two quarters, Harajuku plans to open 10 outlets across new neighbourhoods in Delhi NCR and Mumbai. It is also preparing to enter Bengaluru and Chandigarh. In addition, the company aims to make its central kitchens in Mumbai and Bengaluru operational by December 2026. These facilities will supply Harajuku Bakehouse outlets and support packaged food production for markets in western and southern India. 
 Since its seed funding round in August 2025, the company has doubled its outlet count and revenue. Mumbai, where the brand began operations in July 2025, now contributes 25 percent of its revenue. The business processes more than 1,000 orders daily across dine-in and delivery channels. 
 Harajuku Bakehouse accounts for over 30 percent of the company’s total revenue. In Delhi NCR, the brand sells more than 1,000 loaves of bread each week through quick commerce platform Blinkit. Harajuku plans to extend the Bakehouse format to additional metropolitan markets as it expands its presence in India’s food and beverage sector.

 Nandani Creation Accelerates Jaipur Kurti Expansion with Four New Stores 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 13, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 Nandani Creation Limited, the company behind women's Indian wear brand Jaipur Kurti, has opened four retail stores in a single day under Project 50, its expansion initiative aimed at increasing its store network from 18 to 50 by March 31, 2027. 
 The newly opened outlets are located at DT Mega Mall in Gurgaon, Jammu, Pacific Mall in Jaipur, and Rajouri Garden in Delhi. The openings mark a step forward in the company's efforts to expand its retail footprint and strengthen its presence across key markets. 
 Announced in September 2026, Project 50 focuses on expanding Jaipur Kurti's exclusive brand outlets while integrating its physical stores with its direct-to-consumer (D2C) platform and online marketplaces. The company is also investing in product development, technology adoption, artificial intelligence-led business insights, analytics, and inventory management to improve operational efficiency and support its growth plans. 
 Jaipur Kurti operates through company-owned, company-operated (COCO) and franchise-owned, franchise-operated (FOFO) stores. Its retail presence also extends to departmental stores and shop-in-shop formats. The brand's retail partners include Shoppers Stop, Reliance Trends, Avantara, Kalanikethan, Reliance Centro, Fashion Factory and Lulu Malls. 
 In the online segment, Jaipur Kurti sells through platforms such as Myntra, AJIO, Nykaa, Flipkart and Tata CLiQ, alongside its official website and mobile application. The company has also entered the quick-commerce segment through Swiggy Instamart, expanding its distribution channels. 
 Anuj Mundhra, Chairman and Managing Director, Nandani Creation Limited said , “Project 50 is moving from vision to execution. Opening four stores in a single day is an encouraging milestone and reflects our determination to translate our growth ambitions into measurable progress. Our objective is not simply to expand our retail footprint, but to build a scalable and integrated business that delivers stronger customer reach, better operating efficiency, and sustainable growth. As we move towards our target of 50 stores by March 2027, disciplined execution and long-term value creation will remain at the heart of our strategy.” 
 Founded in 2012, Nandani Creation Limited is a Jaipur-based, online-first fashion company specialising in women's Indian wear. Its portfolio includes Jaipur Kurti, Amaiva – By Jaipur Kurti, Jaipur Kurti Luxe and Desi Fusion. Headquartered in Jaipur, the company operates through a combination of digital commerce platforms and physical retail outlets as it continues to expand its market presence.

 aiqa Expands Into Direct-to-Consumer Healthcare With New Wellness Plans 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 12, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 Health and wellness platform aiqa has entered the direct-to-consumer (D2C) healthcare market, marking a shift from its employer- and partner-led business model to direct consumer engagement. After operating exclusively through employers and business partners for six years, the company is now expanding its services to individuals through a dedicated online platform. 
 Through its new website, aiqa will provide consumers with health plans and preventive healthcare programmes. Its first D2C offering is a doctor-led weight management programme, with additional healthcare and wellness services expected to be introduced in the coming months. 
 Backed by Eleven, aiqa currently generates approximately Rs 100 crore in revenue and adds nearly 1 lakh members every month across more than 500 cities. The move into D2C is expected to help the company establish direct relationships with consumers while broadening access to its healthcare services beyond employer-sponsored and partner-led channels. 
 To support its new business direction, the company has introduced an updated brand identity and a redesigned website. The new platform will serve as the primary digital channel for its consumer-facing healthcare services, allowing individuals to access its offerings without relying on employer or business partnerships. 
 Alongside its D2C expansion, aiqa has appointed Anuj Arora as Chief Executive Officer to lead its partner- and employer-focused business. Arora brings 23 years of professional experience across India, Southeast Asia and Hong Kong. He previously served as Executive Vice President and Business Head at MediBuddy. His experience also includes leading Monster's India small and medium-sized business (SMB) division and its operations in the Philippines and Hong Kong. 
 The company's consumer strategy builds on the healthcare infrastructure, operational capabilities, and member base developed through its existing business. While aiqa will continue serving employers and partners, its D2C model is intended to reach individuals seeking more proactive and personalised healthcare solutions. 
 Weight management and preventive healthcare will form the initial focus of the consumer platform, with plans to expand into other wellness and personalised healthcare services over time.

 Zero-Sugar Beverage Brand Sorry Sugar Names New CEO to Drive Expansion 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 08, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 Zero-added-sugar beverage brand Sorry Sugar has appointed Palash Arneja as its Founder and Chief Executive Officer, strengthening its leadership team as the company prepares for its next phase of growth. 
 Arneja, who previously incubated the brand through Wolfpack Labs, will now take charge of the company’s product innovation, distribution expansion, and overall business growth strategy. 
 The appointment comes shortly after Sorry Sugar secured $1 million in seed funding, led by the Dhanuka family and Amishi London. The fresh capital is expected to support the brand’s expansion plans and category development initiatives. 
 Before joining Sorry Sugar in a leadership capacity, Arneja founded BLA BLI BLU, a venture that, according to the company, achieved a scale of Rs 1,000 crore in less than a year. He has also held positions at Unikon.ai, Deloitte, and HSBC, bringing experience across entrepreneurship, consulting, and financial services. 
 Currently, Sorry Sugar operates in the flavored coffee segment, offering products formulated with zero added sugar, prebiotic fibre, and functional nutrition benefits. The brand uses monk fruit as a natural sweetening ingredient alongside prebiotic fibre to create beverages targeted at health-conscious consumers. 
 As part of its growth roadmap, the company plans to strengthen its presence across both online and offline retail channels while expanding beyond coffee into additional everyday consumption categories. In his new role, Arneja will oversee product development, market expansion, and long-term business strategy. 
 Initially incubated under Wolfpack Labs, Sorry Sugar aims to build a wider portfolio focused on reducing added sugar in daily diets while increasing its footprint across the Indian food and beverage market. 
 The leadership transition reflects the company’s ambition to scale operations and broaden its offerings as consumer demand for healthier beverage alternatives continues to grow in India.

 SORRY SUGAR Appoints Palash Arneja as Founder and CEO to Drive Expansion 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 06, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 SORRY SUGAR, a zero-added-sugar beverage and consumer brand, has announced the appointment of Palash Arneja as its Founder and Chief Executive Officer, as the company looks to accelerate growth and expand its presence in India’s fast-growing better-for-you products market. 
 The leadership announcement comes at a time when consumers are increasingly seeking healthier alternatives without compromising on taste, creating new opportunities for brands focused on wellness-driven innovation. 
 Arneja, who previously built BLA BLI BLU into a Rs 1,000 crore brand within a year, has been associated with SORRY SUGAR since its incubation alongside Wolfpack Labs. In his new role, he will oversee the company’s long-term vision, product development, market expansion, and business strategy. 
 Built around the philosophy, “Break up with sugar, not the sweetness,” SORRY SUGAR aims to make zero-added-sugar products more accessible to consumers by offering alternatives that combine indulgent taste with a health-conscious approach. 
 The brand’s products are formulated using monk fruit, a naturally derived sweetener, along with prebiotic fibre, allowing it to deliver beverages and other offerings that cater to changing consumer preferences for healthier everyday consumption. 
 Palash Arneja, Founder & CEO, SORRY SUGAR said , “Consumers shouldn’t have to choose between health and taste. That belief sits at the heart of SORRY SUGAR. We want to make zero-added-sugar choices accessible, mainstream and genuinely enjoyable. The opportunity is much larger than a single product or category - we are on a mission to change how India consumes sweetness. Our vision is to build SORRY SUGAR into one of India’s most exciting new-age consumer brands, with the ambition to take it global.” 
 The appointment comes as the company prepares for its next stage of expansion, bringing together product innovation, branding, distribution, and business growth under a unified strategy. SORRY SUGAR currently operates in the flavoured coffee segment, offering a portfolio that is zero added sugar, fibre-rich, and prebiotic. 
 Going forward, the company plans to strengthen its presence across both online and offline channels while expanding beyond coffee into additional everyday consumption categories. The broader goal is to build a consumer platform focused on reducing added sugar consumption without compromising on the flavours and experiences consumers enjoy. 
 With increasing awareness around health and nutrition, SORRY SUGAR is positioning itself to capitalize on demand for functional and better-for-you products. The company’s long-term objective remains centered on transforming consumer habits and creating a new approach to sweetness in everyday diets. 
 The brand summed up its ambition with a clear mission: to redefine how India consumes sweetness – by killing the sugar, not the sweetness.

 Sokora by Yes Madam Expands Across D2C and Online Marketplaces 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 01, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 At-home salon and wellness platform Yes Madam has expanded the availability of its Korean-inspired skincare and haircare brand, Sokora, across direct-to-consumer and e-commerce channels. The move follows growing consumer demand for the range, which was initially introduced through the company’s professional beauty services. 
 The Sokora portfolio includes products such as Korean Glow Day & Nite Cream, Korean Kera-Tress Shampoo & Conditioner, Korean Reset Glow Face Wash, Sunscreen SPF 50, 5-in-1 Face Serum, and 3-in-1 Hair Serum, among others. The products are now available through the Yes Madam app, Sokora’s official website, as well as online marketplaces including Amazon, Flipkart, and Myntra.
 The decision to expand into retail was driven by the strong performance of Sokora’s professional range, which is currently used in several Yes Madam treatments, including the Korean Waxing Ritual, Korean Glow Facial, Korean Body Polishing, and Korean Hydraglo Facial. The brand reported significant customer interest in purchasing the products for personal use, prompting the broader rollout.
 The range has been developed to offer convenient everyday skincare and haircare solutions, with a focus on travel-friendly formats and multifunctional products designed to address a variety of beauty needs.
 While inspired by Korean beauty trends, Sokora has been formulated specifically for Indian consumers. The company stated that the products have been adapted to suit Indian skin and hair types, as well as local climatic conditions, rather than replicating existing Korean formulations.
 Aditya Arya, Co-Founder and CEO, Yes Madam said, “We saw that consumers were increasingly interested in Korean beauty, but there was also a need for products that were better suited to Indian skin, hair and weather conditions. As disruptors in the at-home beauty space, we saw an opportunity to bridge this gap by taking inspiration from Korean beauty while developing Sokora around the needs of Indian consumers. We have also focused on making the range convenient for everyday use. The strong response to our professional range gave us the confidence to now make Sokora available to consumers for use at home as well.” 
 With the retail expansion of Sokora, Yes Madam aims to strengthen its presence in the beauty and wellness market by combining service-led expertise with a growing portfolio of consumer products. The company plans to continue introducing new offerings aligned with evolving customer preferences and beauty trends.

 Carpediem Healthcare Launches Direct-to-Consumer Wellness Platform in India 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 01, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 Carpediem Healthcare has announced its entry into India’s growing nutraceutical sector, leveraging more than three decades of experience across international healthcare markets. The company is introducing a portfolio of lifestyle and wellness supplements aimed at addressing the evolving health and wellness needs of Indian consumers. 
 The launch comes amid rising consumer interest in preventive healthcare, nutrition, fitness, sleep, and overall wellbeing. As awareness around wellness products continues to increase, consumers are seeking greater transparency regarding ingredients, product formulations, and the intended benefits of supplements before making purchasing decisions.
 To address this shift, Carpediem Healthcare is adopting a direct-to-consumer (D2C) strategy, enabling customers to access its product range through digital channels. The platform is designed to provide detailed information about product ingredients and formulations while allowing the company to engage directly with consumers and gather feedback.
 Sonnnjay R. Singh, Founder & Managing Director, Carpediem Healthcare , said, “ Today’s generation is perhaps the most informed, aware and ambitious we have ever seen. They don’t just want to do well—they want to be the best version of themselves. They read, research, question and understand what they are putting into their bodies, and they expect the brands they choose to meet those same high standards. Whether it is their career, fitness, sleep or everyday wellbeing, there is a constant desire to perform better and live better. At Carpediem Healthcare, we want to support that ambition with thoughtfully developed products, clear information and a brand that grows alongside this new generation of consumers.”
 The company stated that its product development process focuses on selecting ingredients with specific functions and combining them into formulations tailored to particular wellness requirements. Alongside product innovation, Carpediem is emphasizing consumer education by providing accessible information to help customers make informed decisions about supplement purchases.
 As part of its long-term growth strategy, the company plans to use consumer insights and feedback to guide future product development across lifestyle and wellness categories. Carpediem Healthcare also intends to expand its digital footprint and introduce additional formulations as it strengthens its presence in the Indian nutraceutical market.

 Zigly Pet Care, which describes itself as India’s first omnichannel pet care brand, has acquired Prolife Speciality Vet Clinic in Malad, Mumbai, as part of its strategy to strengthen its veterinary healthcare network and expand its pet care ecosystem across the country. 
 The acquisition marks Zigly Pet Care’s third strategic buyout in the veterinary care segment and is expected to support the company’s plans to build a broader network of specialised pet healthcare facilities. The company said the clinic is expected to transition into a 24x7 facility within the next nine to twelve months. 
 Established in 2000 and managed by Dr. S. M. Gadge, Prolife Speciality Vet Clinic has developed a strong presence in Mumbai’s pet healthcare market, offering services including outpatient consultations, diagnostics, surgery, endoscopy, pathology, and pharmacy support. The clinic has treated nearly 20,000 pets and reports an annual recurring revenue (ARR) of Rs 4.36 crore. 
 Following the acquisition, the clinic will continue to operate with its existing team of veterinarians, centre manager, and support staff to ensure uninterrupted care for current customers and their pets. 
 Saurabh Jain, Chief Executive Officer, Zigly Pet Care, said, “India’s pet care industry is evolving rapidly, with pet parents increasingly seeking specialised healthcare backed by clinical expertise and round the clock support. Prolife Speciality Vet Clinic has earned the trust of Mumbai’s pet parent community over more than two decades, making it an ideal partner in our growth journey. As we plan to transform this into a 24x7 facility and integrating it with the Zigly Pet Care ecosystem, we are expanding access to advanced veterinary care while strengthening trusted our ability to deliver a seamless pet parenting experience. This acquisition also reflects our long-term strategy of scaling high-quality veterinary services through strategic partnerships with respected clinicians across the country.” 
 The addition of the Malad-based clinic further strengthens Zigly Pet Care’s veterinary presence in Mumbai and expands its access to specialised pet healthcare services. The latest acquisition follows the company’s earlier acquisitions of Small Animal Clinic & Surgical Centre in Khar West and Dr. Santa’s Pet Clinic. 
 According to the company, these acquisitions are aimed at creating a wider network of veterinary professionals while improving access to consultations, diagnostics, and treatment services for pet owners. The strategy also seeks to bring specialised veterinary expertise closer to neighbourhood communities and enhance continuity of care for pets requiring long-term medical attention.

 Oziva, the nutrition and wellness brand now wholly owned by Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL), reported strong topline growth in FY26, although rising marketing investments and employee stock option costs weighed on profitability during the fiscal year.
 Oziva’s revenue from operations increased 80 percent to Rs 463.4 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 257.8 crore in FY25. 
 The company derives its revenue from a portfolio of nutrition and wellness products, including plant-based supplements, protein products, vitamins, and solutions focused on skin and hair health. Product sales remained the sole contributor to operating revenue during the year.
 Domestic sales continued to drive the business, contributing Rs 454 crore in FY26, up from Rs 257 crore in the previous fiscal year. The company also recorded growth in international markets, where revenue rose to Rs 8.3 crore, compared with Rs 8.3 lakh in FY25.
 Including Rs 4.1 crore generated through non-operating activities, Oziva’s total income stood at Rs 467.5 crore for the fiscal year. 
 On the expenditure side, advertising and promotional spending remained the company’s largest cost component. Marketing expenditure more than doubled to Rs 246.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 119.8 crore in FY25, accounting for over half of the company’s total expenses.
 The cost of materials consumed increased 63 percent to Rs 116 crore, while employee benefit expenses nearly doubled to Rs 45.4 crore. This figure included Rs 22 crore in cash-settled employee stock option (ESOP) costs, significantly higher than the Rs 7 crore recorded in the previous year. Transportation and logistics expenses also rose 57 percent to Rs 36.9 crore.
 The increase in spending impacted profitability, resulting in a sharp rise in losses. Oziva reported a net loss of Rs 18.5 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 4.2 crore in FY25. The company noted that cash-settled ESOP expenses contributed significantly to the loss as employees exercised stock options following changes in ownership. Excluding the Rs 22 crore ESOP-related cost, Oziva would have reported an estimated profit of around Rs 3.5 crore.
 At the end of FY26, the company’s cash and bank balance stood at Rs 8.8 crore, down 67 percent year-on-year, while current assets totaled Rs 106 crore. 
 The financial performance comes ahead of a major ownership transition. In February 2026, Hindustan Unilever acquired the remaining 49 percent stake in Oziva for Rs 824 crore, making the company a wholly owned subsidiary. HUL had initially purchased a 51 percent stake in the nutrition brand in December 2022 for Rs 264.28 crore. 
 The latest transaction valued Oziva at approximately Rs 1,682 crore, representing a significant increase from the valuation implied during HUL’s initial investment.

 Bewakoof, the direct-to-consumer (D2C) fashion and lifestyle brand owned by the Aditya Birla Group, recorded strong revenue growth in FY26, although its losses continued to widen during the fiscal year ended March 2026.
 The company’s operating revenue increased 40.5 percent to Rs 243 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 173 crore in FY25. 
 Known for its range of fashion and lifestyle products, including T-shirts, hoodies, bags, and phone covers, Bewakoof continued to derive the majority of its income from product sales during the year. 
 On the expenditure side, the cost of materials consumed remained the company’s largest expense category. Material costs rose 45.7 percent year-on-year to Rs 134 crore, up from Rs 92 crore in FY25.
 Employee benefit expenses increased 7.7 percent to Rs 28 crore, while marketing and promotional spending grew 26.5 percent to Rs 62 crore, reflecting continued investments in customer acquisition and brand visibility. In contrast, transportation and handling expenses declined 17.1 percent to Rs 29 crore, compared to Rs 35 crore in the previous fiscal year.
 The company also reported a significant increase in depreciation expenses, which nearly tripled to Rs 16.6 crore from Rs 6 crore in FY25. Other operating expenses rose 66.1 percent to Rs 66.4 crore, up from Rs 40 crore a year earlier.
 Overall, Bewakoof’s total expenditure climbed 35.5 percent to Rs 336 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 248 crore in the previous fiscal. 
 Despite the sharp rise in revenue, the company reported a wider net loss. Bewakoof’s loss increased 19.4 percent to Rs 87.4 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 73.2 crore in FY25. 
 However, some profitability indicators showed improvement. The company’s EBITDA loss narrowed slightly to Rs 59.8 crore from Rs 60.7 crore in the previous year, while its EBITDA margin improved to -24.6 percent from -35.1 percent. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) also improved to -63.4 percent, compared with -96.6 percent in FY25.
 Operational efficiency improved marginally as well. Bewakoof spent Rs 1.38 to generate every Rs 1 of operating revenue during FY26, compared with Rs 1.43 in the previous year. 
 The company’s balance sheet reflected moderate growth in assets, with total current assets rising to Rs 91.1 crore at the end of FY26 from Rs 84.8 crore a year earlier. Cash and bank balances also increased slightly to Rs 22 lakh, compared with Rs 18 lakh in FY25.
 FY26 was also a significant year for the company from a leadership perspective. Prabhkiran Singh, co-founder of Bewakoof, stepped down from the business in February 2026, ending a 14-year association with the company. His departure came nearly three years after Aditya Birla Digital Fashion Ventures (ABDFVL) acquired a majority stake in Bewakoof in February 2023 through TMRW, the Aditya Birla Group’s digital-first fashion and lifestyle venture.

 The Indian Garage Co (TIGC), a direct-to-consumer (D2C) fashion brand focused on men's apparel, recorded a moderate rise in revenue during FY26 amid increasing competition in India's online fashion market. While the company continued to expand its topline, its losses widened as spending on marketing, operations, and workforce increased during the year. 
 TIGC's revenue from operations grew 15 percent to Rs 234.6 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 204.2 crore in FY25. 
 The company, which designs, manufactures, and sells men's fashion products under its own labels, generated its operating revenue entirely through product sales. 
 Including other income of Rs 2.95 crore, TIGC's total income reached Rs 237.5 crore during FY26, up from Rs 206.9 crore in the previous fiscal year. 
 On the expenditure front, raw material costs remained the company's largest expense category. Material costs increased 13 percent to Rs 117.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 104 crore a year earlier. 
 The company significantly increased its investment in marketing and brand visibility during the year. Advertising and promotional expenses climbed to Rs 29.3 crore, more than double the Rs 14 crore spent in FY25, reflecting heightened competition among D2C fashion brands.
 Job work charges, covering outsourced manufacturing and production activities, stood at Rs 39.5 crore. Employee benefit expenses also increased 24 percent year-on-year to Rs 21 crore.
 Additional costs, including depreciation and amortisation, finance charges, legal and professional fees, travel expenditure, and other operational expenses, pushed the company's total spending to Rs 276.1 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 237.5 crore in FY25, representing a 16 percent increase.
 As expenses continued to grow faster than revenue, TIGC's losses widened during the fiscal year. The company reported a net loss of Rs 28.7 crore, up 27 percent from Rs 22.6 crore in FY25.
 Operational efficiency metrics also reflected the pressure on profitability. The company spent Rs 1.18 to generate every rupee of operating revenue during FY26, compared with Rs 1.16 in the previous year. Its EBITDA margin improved slightly to -5.12 percent from -6 percent, while return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at -12.61 percent.
 TIGC received a major boost in October 2023 when Aditya Birla Group's TMRW invested approximately Rs 155 crore in the business, securing a 51 percent stake. TMRW has also expanded its presence in the D2C fashion segment through investments in brands such as Bewakoof.
 The company's FY26 performance highlights the evolving dynamics of India's D2C fashion sector, where brands are facing rising customer acquisition costs and increasing competition.

During his tenure, the business expanded significantly, with Bombay Shaving Company becoming the second-largest men’s trimmer brand in India. He also played a key role in scaling the company’s online business while improving profitability. Prior to joining Visage Lines, Gupta held roles at PepsiCo and Hindustan Unilever and was involved in building brands such as Too Yumm! and The Gift Studio for the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group. 
 Varun Gupta, Chief Marketing Officer, Bombay Shaving Company said, “The opportunity ahead for Bombay Shaving Company is to build on the strong equity we have created by being bold and defiant of the category and societal codes over the past few years. As we scale Bombay Shaving Company and Bombae, the opportunity now is to turbocharge this beyond the top urban centres and build a unified voice that cuts across grooming and other categories and brands. Our focus will be on deepening our consumer connect and sharpening our brand propositions to make them culturally relevant, differentiated and commercially strong. Excited for what’s ahead.” 
 Alongside Gupta’s appointment, Jasmeet Singh will lead the next phase of the company’s ecommerce strategy as Senior Vice President, Ecommerce.  In his new position, Singh will oversee ecommerce operations across marketplaces, quick commerce platforms, and beauty commerce channels for the company’s portfolio of brands. His responsibilities will include strengthening channel strategies, identifying new growth opportunities, and driving scale across the digital business. 
 Jasmeet Singh, Senior Vice President, Ecommerce, Visage Lines Personal Care Pvt. Ltd. shared, "Digital commerce is increasingly shaping how consumers discover, evaluate and purchase personal care products, making it an important growth lever for brands at scale. Visage Lines has a strong and diverse portfolio, with significant opportunities to build greater depth across marketplaces, quick commerce and beauty commerce. My focus will be on creating sharper channel strategies and building win-win propositions for consumers, customers and the brands, with a strong impetus on outside-in learning. We will focus on strengthening the ecommerce ecosystem across the portfolio and building sustainable digital businesses as Visage Lines enters its next phase of growth.” 
 Through brands including Bombay Shaving Company, Bombae, and 100Days, Visage Lines has established a presence across men’s grooming, women’s hair removal, and hair styling categories. Its products are available through D2C channels, ecommerce marketplaces, quick commerce platforms, beauty commerce networks, and offline retail outlets.

 MyRx said it is developing a shared healthcare infrastructure model that connects patients, doctors, and enterprise partners through a unified platform. By combining clinical expertise with technology-driven consultation allocation, workflow monitoring, and audit systems, the company seeks to help healthcare partners expand patient access while maintaining operational transparency and accountability. 
 The Hyderabad-based startup currently handles approximately 35,000 teleconsultations daily and reports 15 percent month-on-month growth. Its platform brings together doctor availability, teleconsultation services, electronic prescriptions, and workflow management tools, enabling enterprises to integrate healthcare services into their existing offerings. 
 As part of its growth strategy, MyRx plans to expand its doctor network, strengthen clinical quality and technology systems, and simplify integration processes for enterprise partners. The company also intends to further develop its digital clinic model and establish additional healthcare partnerships aimed at connecting remote consultations with local healthcare access points. 
 According to MyRx, the platform has achieved a 95th-percentile first doctor-call response time of 30 seconds and a 95th-percentile overall workflow turnaround time of 179 seconds. The company said these metrics reflect its focus on delivering timely healthcare services while scaling operations.
